flights.recommendation: Ryanair / easyJet from Frankfurt (FRA) or Frankfurt-Hahn (HHN) to Barcelona (BCN)
flights.tip: Book 2-3 months ahead. Ryanair from HHN is cheapest (~€40-60 each way). Check Skyscanner/Google Flights. Pack light — only carry-on.

accommodation.recommendation: Hostel or budget hotel in El Raval or Eixample Esquerra

options.name: Generator Hostel Barcelona
options.vibe: Social hostel, rooftop pool, walking distance to Ramblas

options.name: Hostal Centric Barcelona
options.why: Good if you want privacy without hostel dorms

daily_itinerary.title: Arrival + Gothic Quarter
activities: Arrive at BCN airport — take Aerobús (€5.90) to Plaça Catalunya (35 min)
Check in, drop bags
Afternoon: Walk through Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) — narrow medieval streets, Plaça Reial, Barcelona Cathedral
Evening: Tapas crawl on Carrer de Blai — pintxos at €2-3 each. Try Bodega La Palma or La Tasqueta de Blai
Dinner: Can Culleretes (est. 1786!) — oldest restaurant in Barcelona, affordable set menu

daily_itinerary.title: Gaudí: Sagrada Família
activities: Morning: **Sagrada Família** — pre-book tickets online (€26) for 9am, less crowded. ABSOLUTE MUST-SEE for architecture
Take the Passion Facade tower if you can — best views
Lunch: La Paradeta (Sagrada Família branch) — market-style seafood, pick your own, pay by weight
Afternoon: Walk through **Sant Pau Recinte Modernista** — former hospital, stunning Modernist architecture, €15, usually quiet
Evening: Dinner at El Quim de la Boqueria — inside La Boqueria market, best at lunch actually. For dinner try Bar del Pla in Born

daily_itinerary.title: Gaudí: Park Güell + Gràcia
activities: Morning: **Park Güell** — pre-book tickets (€10) for 10am. Gaudí's colorful park with incredible mosaic benches
Walk down through **Gràcia neighborhood** — bohemian vibe, less touristy, great little plazas
Lunch in Gràcia: La Pubilla or Can Xurrades — authentic Catalan, €12-15 menu del día
Afternoon: **Casa Vicens** (Gaudí's first house, €18) — colorful Moorish-inspired masterpiece, less crowded than Casa Batlló
Evening: Relax at Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia — great people-watching, cheap drinks at local bars

daily_itinerary.title: Casa Batlló + Passeig de Gràcia
activities: Morning: **Casa Batlló** (€35-43 with audio guide) — the most magical Gaudí house. BOOK AHEAD. The blue-tiled atrium is breathtaking
Then walk Passeig de Gràcia — see **Casa Milà (La Pedrera)** from outside (€24 if you want to go up to the rooftop)
Lunch: La Rita (Carrer d'Aragó) — excellent €14 menu del día, 3 courses + drink
Afternoon: **Palau de la Música Catalana** — book a 1-hour guided tour (€20), stunning Modernist concert hall by Domènech i Montaner
Evening: Dinner at Cal Pep in El Born — legendary tapas, queue early (opens 7pm), €30-40 well spent

daily_itinerary.title: Montjuïc + Catalan Food
activities: Morning: **Montjuïc Castle** — take the cable car up (€12 each way), incredible views of the port and city
Walk down through **Joan Miró Foundation** (€13) — beautiful building, amazing art, peaceful garden
Lunch: **Mercat de la Llibertat** in Gràcia — local market, grab fresh food, much less touristy than Boqueria
Afternoon: CaixaForum (free entry with some cards) — former textile factory turned art center
Evening: **Spanish Cooking Class** (€40-50) — affordable ones at Barcelona Cooking or Cook & Taste. Learn paella and tapas!

daily_itinerary.title: El Born + Picasso + Barceloneta
activities: Morning: **Picasso Museum** (€12, free Thu evenings) — incredible collection of early Picasso, in beautiful Gothic palaces
Walk through **El Born** — Santa Maria del Mar church (free, breathtaking Gothic), El Born CCM (cultural center)
Lunch: Can Paixano (La Xampanyeria) — legendary cava bar, €2-3 sandwiches + cava, very local, chaotic and amazing
Afternoon: Walk to **Barceloneta beach** — grab a drink at a chiringuito (beach bar), swim if it's hot
Evening: Dinner at **Can Majó** (Barceloneta) — best paella in Barcelona, €20-25, book ahead

daily_itinerary.title: Day Trip: Montserrat
activities: Full day: **Montserrat Monastery** — take R5 train from Plaça d'Espanya (€25 round trip + cremallera/funicular)
See the Black Madonna (La Moreneta), explore the basilica
Hike to **Sant Jeroni** — highest peak, 2h walk, INCREDIBLE views of all Catalonia
Listen to the Escolania boys' choir (sings at 1pm Mon-Fri)
Bring your own picnic lunch — the monastery food is expensive and average
Back to Barcelona by 6-7pm
Evening: Light dinner — try **La Flauta** on Carrer d'Aribau, €15-20, amazing montaditos (small sandwiches)

daily_itinerary.title: Modernisme + Sant Antoni
activities: Morning: **Hospital de Sant Pau** — you walked past it on day 2, but this time do the full guided tour (€15). Unesco site, jaw-dropping
Then: **Recinte Modernista Sant Pau** gardens — free to wander the outdoor areas
Lunch: **Mercat de Sant Antoni** — recently renovated, amazing food hall, much cheaper than Boqueria. Try the jamón and cheese counter
Afternoon: Walk **Rambla del Raval** — less touristy version of La Rambla, see the famous Botero cat statue
Evening: Dinner at **El Nacional** (Passeig de Gràcia, 24) — stunning Modernist former garage turned food hall, 4 different restaurants inside, mid-range €25-35

daily_itinerary.title: Last full day — Free + Farewell
activities: Morning: Visit **Palau Güell** (€12) — Gaudí's early mansion for the Güell family, incredible rooftop with chimneys
Or revisit a favorite spot / do unfinished business
Lunch: **Market crawl** — hit Boqueria (touristy but worth it) for a last taste: El Pinotxo bar, jamón, fresh juice
Afternoon: **Free time** — shopping in El Born (boutiques), or **Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya** (MNAC, €12) on Montjuïc for Romanesque art collection (one of the best in the world)
Sunset: **Bunkers del Carmel** — free, best sunset view in Barcelona, take bus 119 up. Bring a drink and snacks
Farewell dinner: **Can Solé** in Barceloneta — traditional Catalan, family-run since 1905, €30-40

daily_itinerary.title: Departure
activities: Morning: Last walk, buy souvenirs at **Santa Caterina Market** (beautiful colorful roof, less crowded)
Aerobús back to BCN airport (€5.90, every 5-10 min)
Arrive at airport 2h before flight

food_highlights.where: Literally everywhere, but best at Cal Pep
Most bars in Gràcia and Eixample — look for €12-15 menus

architecture_must_see: Palau Reial / Plaça Reial (free, Gothic Quarter)
Recinte Modernista Sant Pau gardens (free outdoor)
free_activities: La Boqueria market (walking is free, eating costs)

transportation.airport: Aerobús (€5.90) or metro L9 Sud (€5.50) — both ~35 min to center
transportation.metro: T-Casual card: 10 rides for €11.35 (single ride €2.55). Buy at any station
transportation.walking: Barcelona is very walkable — most attractions are within 30 min walk
transportation.bike: Bicing (€50/year) not for tourists. Rent a bike ~€10/day from shops in El Born

practical_tips: August is HOT (30-35°C) and packed with tourists. Book Sagrada/Casa Batlló at least 1 week ahead
Siesta: many shops close 2-5pm, but attractions stay open. Use afternoon for indoor activities
Pickpockets: keep phone/wallet in front pockets or zipped bag. Avoid La Rambla at night alone
Language: Catalan first, Spanish second. 'Bon dia' and 'Gràcies' go a long way
Water: tap water is safe but tastes chlorinated. Carry a bottle and refill at public fountains
Tipping: not expected but appreciated. Round up or leave 5-10% for great service
Neighborhood safety: El Raval is fine during day, avoid dark side streets at night. El Born and Gràcia are very safe
Best free view: Bunkers del Carmel. Go at sunset. Bus 119 from Alfons X metro
